notes.title: Engine Update: Better lighting AND better performance?
notes.notes:
The Godot Engine 4.4 has been [url=https://godotengine.org/releases/4.4/]released[/url] and comes with some long awaited, exciting features! 
Also in this release: Bugfixes, Optimizations and preparation for Internationalization and Sword Beach.

[h2]Performance[/h2]
[list]
[*][b]No more stuttering during runtime![/b] Shaders are now pre-compiled during loading of a scene, which (mostly) prevents stuttering while exploring the museum.
[*]The typewriter effect at the Audio Guide got an overhaul and is now more lightweight
[*]Optimized LOD's
[*]Optimized obstacle meshes at the Omaha Beach scene
[*]Reworked Juno Beach, which resulted in [b]~5x more fps[/b] in some areas
[/list]

[h2]Graphics[/h2]
[list]
[*]Lightmaps support now directional data aka normal maps, which results in more detailed objects
[/list]

[h2]Gameplay[/h2]
[list]
[*]Added a new scene for first time users, to choose their VR Experience Level and apply some presets accordingly
[*]Fixed a bug in Operation Albany, where other paratroopers wouldn't get deleted, after the scene ends. Which caused paratroopers lying around in all other scenes (xD)
[/list]

Next Stop: [b]Sword Beach[/b]

notes.title: Two years of development
notes.notes:
In June 2022, after visiting Normandy for the first time, I began to think about creating a Virtual Reality Museum about it. This idea matured over several months, and finally, in December 2022, I started developing the first bits for it.

I visited Normandy two more times in 2024 to create 3D scans and 360° imagery, aiming to make the museum as realistic as possible.

I made several (costly) mistakes, but learned more in those 2 years than in the 5 before. It was a wild ride with lots of ups and downs, and I was several times on the verge of giving up, not knowing if anybody had any interest in this kind of project. But I had put too much effort into it to let it down. So, here we are now.

I hope you all enjoy the museum and are excited about what’s coming next year. Until then, I wish everyone a Merry Christmas and a Happy New Year!

- Daniel

notes.title: Quest 3, Options and more...
notes.notes:
[list]
[*] Fixed a rendering bug with Quest 3's, where the image appeared blurry/low quality. "Variable Rate Shading" caused this, which is a technique to render parts of the image at lower quality, to improve performance. VRS is now an option to turn on in the options menu (default: off)
[*] Ability to set antialiasing in the options
[*] Rebuilt options menu: added tabs to categorize each option
[*] Redesigned D-Day Map at the Entrance
[*] Redesigned World War 2 Timeline at the Entrance
[*] Added labels to some of the activations points, that lead to other scenes
[*] Faster loading times
[/list]

notes.title: Now Available!
notes.notes:
After 2 years in development, the D-Day VR Museum is now available for everyone in Early Access!

[previewyoutube=odFKlMdg2nI;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]The Early Access Version includes:[/h3]
[list]
[*] 3 of the 5 invasion beaches
[*] 1 bonus scene (Mission Albany)
[*] over 2 hours voice overs
[*] over 1 hour original video footage
[*] over 150 original pictures
[*] several 3D scans from Normandy
[*] several 360° pictures from Normandy
[/list]

Please report any feedback or bugs in the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/2512870/discussions/]Steam Community Discussions[/url].

I want to thank everyone who has already wishlisted the museum, and I encourage you to tell everyone about it!

notes.title: Early Access
notes.notes:
Join me on November 1st, 2024, for a special Steam event celebrating the Early Access release of the D-Day VR Museum! After 2 years of dedicated development, i'm thrilled to invite you to experience a one-of-a-kind virtual journey back to the historic events of D-Day.

Immerse yourself in the sights and sounds of June 6, 1944, as you walk through recreated environments, witness key moments, and gain a deeper understanding of the sacrifices made by brave soldiers on that fateful day. This event marks the beginning of a groundbreaking virtual reality experience that blends traditional museum exhibits with cutting-edge technology.

- Daniel
